objective: Add a code-backed, metadata-only Cloud Network + DNS cell guardrail for Cilium default-deny, Envoy fail-closed authz/mTLS, CoreDNS pod-mode safety, and no default cross-cell traffic; reconcile Cloud Network and Cloud Network DNS manifests to truthful local-foundation claims only.

best_practice_sources.name: Cilium default-deny policy documentation
best_practice_sources.takeaway: Network policy needs an explicit enforcement posture; this slice models default-deny ingress/egress rather than implicit default allow.

best_practice_sources.name: Kubernetes NetworkPolicy concepts
best_practice_sources.takeaway: Ingress/egress isolation is policy-selected and additive; the guardrail requires explicit DNS egress exception and forbids broad cross-cell defaults.

best_practice_sources.name: Envoy external authorization filter
best_practice_sources.takeaway: Network edge authorization belongs at the proxy boundary; the guardrail requires Envoy external authorization and fail-closed behavior.

best_practice_sources.name: CoreDNS Kubernetes plugin documentation
best_practice_sources.takeaway: CoreDNS pod modes have security posture implications; the guardrail permits disabled/verified and rejects insecure pod mode.

findings: The slice adds one small guardrail value object and tests instead of inventing runtime controllers.
Manifest truth-down deletes broad runtime/SLO/DR overclaims and preserves only code-backed local foundation claims.

Cilium/Envoy/CoreDNS posture is modeled as fail-closed metadata: default-deny, explicit DNS exception, no default cross-cell traffic, ext_authz fail-closed, mTLS, and verified/disabled CoreDNS pod mode.
No production/hyperscaler readiness claim is made without live runtime and measurement evidence.

alternatives_named: Add a narrow metadata guardrail plus manifest truth-down
F6_alternatives.selected_rationale: The narrow metadata guardrail adds a durable invariant for the next network foundation step without faking live runtime, SLO, DR, DNS, or provider evidence.
rejected_reasons: Live controllers would touch broad Kubernetes/GitOps/IaC/runtime contracts too early.
Manifest-only truth-down would not add code-backed no-cross-cell/default-deny invariants.

findings: Guardrail rejects secret-like evidence refs and requires fail-closed network posture.
No raw provider credentials, kubeconfigs, DNSSEC keys, TSIG keys, Envoy secrets, Cilium tokens, or tenant payloads are introduced.
